lead.headline: The AI Rout Rolls Into a Second Week: Kospi Sinks Another 4.9% as Seoul Readies a Rescue Fund and Goldman Warns of Up to $80 Billion in Trend-Fund Selling
lead.dek: Asia's chip markets fell again on Monday despite weekend support measures in Seoul and Taipei, leaving Wall Street's Thanksgiving week to start under heavy selling pressure while oil barely reacted to the Gulf strikes.
body: Monday's first sessions after a week of steep global losses brought no relief for chip-heavy Asia. Korea's Kospi was down 4.86% at 4,633.22 at 11:30 a.m. KST on 23 November, adding to Friday's 5.21% fall, with Samsung Electronics down 4.72% and SK hynix down 4.13% by 11:20 a.m. The losses came hours after an emergency Sunday meeting at which Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il said Seoul would prepare a market stabilisation fund to buy index-linked products and ease buyback limits for three months from 24 November; no size or start date was given.

Taiwan, where a blanket ban on short-selling any stock trading below its previous close took effect on Monday, steadied in early trade after the Taiex's worst week since 1991. Tokyo was shut for Labour Thanksgiving Day. Elsewhere the picture was mixed: Australia's ASX 200 recovered from a 0.6% opening drop to trade up 0.1% around midday as miners rallied, Jakarta fell 1.53% with the rupiah at a record low, and Karachi's KSE-100 rose about 0.3%.

For Wall Street, which closed Friday with the S&P 500 at 6,914.90 after a 3.64% one-day drop, positioning is the immediate worry. Goldman Sachs' trading desk said in a Sunday note that trend-following funds could sell up to about $80.6 billion of stocks this week if markets keep falling and roughly $28.6 billion even if they rise, while hedge funds shorted US single stocks at the fastest weekly pace since June 2022. The desk's panic index stood at 9.8 out of 10 on Friday. Ed Yardeni cut his year-end S&P 500 target to 7,500 from 7,900, still about 8.5% above Friday's close.

Oil, by contrast, slipped. Brent traded near $91.96 at 11:00 Singapore time, below Friday's $92.57 settlement, as the equity sell-off outweighed weekend Iranian strikes on Bahrain and a Houthi claim of a hit on Saudi Arabia's Rabigh refinery. Gold rebounded more than 1.5% in Asian trade after its worst week since March. HPE's results after Monday's US close and Dell's on Tuesday are the first fundamental tests of the AI-hardware demand that sits at the centre of the sell-off.

impact.title: What it means for markets
points: Chips remain the epicentre: Samsung and SK hynix lead Korea lower and the Philadelphia Semiconductor index fell 10.73% on Friday, so NVDA, TSMC and memory names set the tone for global indices this week.
Mechanical selling risk is high in a holiday-thinned week: Goldman's CTA estimates and record-low hedge-fund net leverage mean futures flows, not news, can drive SPX and NDX moves.
Policy backstops are arriving in Asia (Taiwan's short ban, Seoul's planned fund) but did not stop Monday's Kospi drop; any US equivalent would be a regime change, and none has been signalled.
Havens are behaving unevenly: Treasuries rallied on Friday and gold bounced on Monday, while oil is trading on demand fears rather than Gulf supply risk.

read.title: The Ledger's Read
paragraphs: The AI sell-off has crossed the weekend intact. Korea's Kospi fell almost another 5% on Monday morning, hours after Seoul promised a stabilisation fund, and Taiwan's new short-selling ban only steadied a market that lost almost a fifth of its value last week. The lesson from Asia is that administrative backstops can slow a slide but not reverse it while the underlying question, how much AI hardware demand is really worth, stays open. That question gets its first answers this week from HPE tonight and Dell on Tuesday, both of which are trying to push higher memory and component costs onto customers with signed orders.

Wall Street's problem in the short run is plumbing more than news. Goldman's estimate that trend-following funds could sell up to $80bn of stocks into a holiday-thinned week, alongside record-low hedge-fund leverage and still-high asset-manager exposure, means futures flows can move indices sharply in either direction. Strategists are trimming targets rather than capitulating, but none of them is calling the low. In this setting, take-private bids such as GTCR's for Global Payments show where private capital sees value, while CCC spreads show where the strain is building.

The Gulf is the risk that markets are choosing not to price. Brent slipped on Monday even after Iran's strikes on Bahrain and a Houthi claim against Rabigh, because demand fear dominates and the US blockade has already removed Iranian barrels. That calm depends on Iran's 14 waiting tankers staying in port and on Trump's post-New Year timetable holding. Watch the 2-year auction and Nigeria's MPC today, Dell on Tuesday, PCE and GDP on Wednesday, OPEC+ and Spain's election on Sunday, and the frontier currencies, from the rupiah to the rand, that are absorbing the stress first.

stories.headline: Wall Street Faces a Holiday Week of Forced Selling Risk: Goldman Sees Up to $80 Billion From Trend Funds as Hedge-Fund Shorting Hits a 2022 High
stories.summary: US stocks enter Thanksgiving week after a seventh straight loss, with the S&P 500 at 6,914.90, the Nasdaq Composite at 22,682.49 and the Dow at 48,216.66 at Friday's 20 Nov close and the VIX at 35.89. A Goldman Sachs desk note on Sunday 22 Nov estimated that trend-following CTAs could sell up to $80.6bn of stocks this week if the slide continues and about $28.6bn even in a rebound, and said hedge funds' US single-stock shorting was the heaviest in a week since June 2022. Yardeni Research cut its year-end S&P target to 7,500 from 7,900. Monday's session follows a further 4.9% drop in Korea's Kospi in Asian trade; no confirmed US futures level was available at press time.
stories.market: SPX, NDX and the SOX are exposed to mechanical futures selling in thin holiday trade; HPE (after Monday's close) and Dell (Tuesday) are the first earnings tests of AI-hardware demand, and the $69bn 2-year Treasury auction on Monday tests the haven bid.

body: The S&P 500 ended Friday 20 November at 6,914.90, down 3.64% on the day, and both it and the Dow are more than 10% below their records, a correction triggered by governance turmoil at Nvidia and an SEC review rather than by earnings. The Nasdaq Composite lost 5.01% on Friday and about 10% for the week.

Positioning now matters as much as news. Goldman's desk estimates CTAs sold about $57bn of equities over the past month and could sell up to $80.6bn more this week in a falling market. Hedge funds were net sellers of global equities for a third week, with short sales outpacing long buying by 1.5 to 1, and fundamental long-short net leverage fell to 42.3%, a one-year low. Asset managers, by contrast, still hold equity-futures exposure in the 82nd percentile of the past decade.

Strategists are trimming rather than capitulating. Yardeni's cut to 7,500 is his second in two months; Goldman's Ben Snider noted the forward P/E has fallen to about 16 times, and Macro Risk Advisors' John Kolovos sees room for another 5% decline before a lasting low.
The week is short: earnings from HPE and Zoom on Monday, Dell, Workday, Autodesk and HP on Tuesday, PCE inflation and Q3 GDP on Wednesday, a market holiday on Thursday and an early close on Friday.

stories.headline: Rate-Setters' Holiday Week: Nigeria's MPC Opens, the SNB Flags Second-Round Inflation and the Treasury Sells $69 Billion of 2-Year Notes Into a Haven Bid
stories.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield closed Friday 20 Nov at 4.92% and the 2-year at 4.63% after a flight to safety, and the Treasury sells $69bn of 2-year notes on Monday 23 Nov as part of $183bn of 2-, 5- and 7-year supply this week. Futures priced about a 90% chance of a 25bp Fed hike on 9 December as of Friday, with October PCE on Wednesday the last major inflation print before the meeting. Abroad, the Central Bank of Nigeria's MPC opens a two-day meeting on 23 Nov with analysts expecting a hold at 23%, and SNB Vice Chairman Antoine Martin said on 22 Nov the bank is watching for second-round effects after Swiss inflation rose to 1.5% in October.
stories.market: The 2-year auction and PCE decide whether Friday's rally in Treasuries holds; a hold in Lagos would keep T-bill yields near 15.5-16% as the naira weakens, and Martin's comments add to talk of a Swiss move from 0% in December.

body: Treasuries were the main beneficiary of Friday's equity rout: the 10-year yield fell 12bp to 4.92%, below 5% for the first time since 10 November, and the 2-year fell 13bp to 4.63%. This week's note supply arrives into a holiday-thinned market.

The Fed's policy range is 3.75%-4.00%, and Friday's pricing still pointed strongly to a December hike after Governor Cook and Philadelphia Fed President Paulson backed further increases. Wednesday brings October PCE, Q3 GDP and durable goods at 14:30 CET.

Outside the US, Nigeria's central bank is expected by United Capital, Standard Chartered and Parthian Securities to hold its policy rate at 23% after September's 350bp cut, with inflation at 14.06% in October. Bank Indonesia's surprise 25bp hike to 6.00% on 18 November has not yet stopped the rupiah's slide. In Switzerland, Martin's interview kept the focus on inflation as the franc stays a haven.

stories.summary: Brent traded near $91.96 a barrel at 11:00 Singapore time on Monday 23 Nov, about 0.65% below Friday's $92.57 settlement, and WTI near $83.01, after Reuters had Brent at $92.29 at 02:16 GMT. The weekend brought Iranian strikes on US-used bases in Bahrain, at least seven tankers hit near Hormuz since 16 Nov, a Trump warning that blockade-runners would be sunk and a Houthi claim of a hit on Saudi Arabia's 400,000 b/d Rabigh refinery, which Riyadh has not confirmed. Reuters said the Rabigh claim limited oil's losses, while the global stock sell-off and surplus forecasts kept prices on the defensive. Natural gas also slipped in Asian trade, Gulf News reported.
stories.market: Brent and WTI are trading demand fear over Gulf supply risk; the OPEC+ meeting on 29 Nov and any attempt by Iran's 14 tankers to run the blockade are the next catalysts, with tanker war-risk premiums and PetroRabigh the most exposed names.

body: Oil's reaction to one of the war's busiest weekends was muted. Brent spent last week falling on an IEA-forecast fourth-quarter surplus of about 2m barrels a day and record flows cited by US officials, ending with a third weekly loss. Monday's Asian trade showed the equity sell-off still dominating.

The supply risks have not gone away. Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they targeted bases in Bahrain used by US forces, and Bahrain reported two wounded and a fire at an industrial site on Sitra, home to Bapco's refinery. Iran is reported to be readying 14 tankers at Kharg to test the US blockade, and President Trump said they would be sunk.

On the Red Sea side, the Houthis claimed a hit on Rabigh, at the western end of Saudi Arabia's route around Hormuz; the Saudi-led coalition reported intercepting missiles and drones but no confirmation of damage. That claim, Reuters said, helped cap the decline.

stories.headline: Likud-Yashar Talks End Without a Deal as the Shekel Posts Its Weakest Close Since 2025
stories.summary: Negotiators for Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar and caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud met for four hours in Herzliya on Sunday 22 Nov but reached no agreement, saying only that they had set out positions and would meet again on an unspecified date. Eisenkot's bloc holds 48 of the 120 Knesset seats, 13 short of a majority, and he has until 6 Dec, with a possible 14-day extension, to form a government; he refuses to serve under Netanyahu, who is pushing a rotation deal.
stories.market: The shekel closed Friday 20 Nov near NIS 3.34 per dollar, its weakest close since September 2025, after a 4.5% weekly drop; it is down more than 8% since the 27 Oct election, and the TA-125 is down 4.7% in November (Times of Israel, 23 Nov).

body: The second round of talks between Yashar and Likud, held at a Herzliya hotel on 22 Nov, followed a first round on 15 Nov. A joint statement said the sides had outlined their positions on a range of substantive issues, and a follow-up meeting is planned.

Likud's conditions for a unity government include excluding Arab parties, rejecting a Palestinian state and a compromise on ultra-Orthodox conscription. Eisenkot's camp remains split between a deal with ultra-Orthodox parties, reliance on Arab parties, which hold 19 seats, or a unity government; on 20 Nov he said he was ready to put an emergency government to parliament rather than let talks drag on.

Currency markets have priced the uncertainty. The shekel was the third-worst performer among 31 widely traded currencies last week, behind Colombia's peso and Brazil's real, while the dollar index was up about 2% in November, the Times of Israel reported on 23 Nov. stories.headline: Iran War, Day 269: Oil Shrugs Off the Bahrain Strikes as Trump Points to a Post-New Year Decision and Dares Tankers to Run the Blockade
stories.summary: Brent slipped in Monday's Asian session, trading near $91.96 a barrel at 11:00 Singapore time on 23 November, about $0.60 below Friday's $92.57 settle, as a global equity sell-off outweighed weekend attacks in the Gulf. Bahrain said an Iranian strike set fire to a civilian industrial site, with smoke seen over Sitra island, home to Bapco's refinery, and on 22 November raised the toll to two wounded; the Revolutionary Guards said they targeted the US-used Riffa and Awali bases and two Patriot radars. In a Fox News interview on 22 November Trump said he was inclined to resume strikes after the New Year if no deal is reached and warned that tankers testing the US blockade would be sunk, as Iran was reported to be readying 14 tankers to try. Seven tankers have been hit in the strait since 16 November, according to the Joint Maritime Information Centre cited by Iran International on 23 November.
stories.market: Brent (BZ=F) traded at $91.96 (-0.65%) and WTI at $83.01 at 11:00 Singapore time on 23 Nov, after a third weekly loss of about 4%; Reuters cited an analyst warning that the shipping attacks are starting to bite as empty tankers pile up. Gulf tanker war-risk cover, Bahrain and Saudi equities and the Bahraini dinar's sovereign risk are the most exposed channels; the OPEC+ meeting on 29 Nov is the next oil-supply catalyst.

body: Oil's first trading session after a weekend of Gulf attacks was a muted one. Reuters put Brent at $92.29 at 02:16 GMT on Monday, 28 cents lower, and Gulf News, citing Trading Economics, had it at about $91.96 by 11:00 Singapore time, with WTI near $83.01. Reuters tied the dip to a broader sell-off driven by doubts over AI-led growth, with South Korea's tech-heavy market down about 4% at the open, and said continuing attacks on Gulf shipping and a Houthi claim against a Saudi refinery limited the losses.

In Bahrain, the interior ministry said Iran hit a civilian industrial facility late on 21 November, causing a fire; AFP reported smoke over Sitra island, which hosts state oil firm Bapco's refinery. On 22 November the ministry said two people were wounded, one critically. The Revolutionary Guards said they aimed missiles and drones at the Riffa and Awali bases used by US forces and struck two Patriot radars. A US official described it as the fourth attempted Iranian attack on Bahrain in about a week, and the UAE condemned it on 22 November.

At sea, UKMTO reported two tankers hit near the strait on 21 November, one by an unidentified projectile and one with engine-room damage, while Iran's army said a third struck a mine after entering a restricted zone. Iran International, citing the Joint Maritime Information Centre, counted seven tankers hit since 16 November; Gulf News reported Hormuz traffic around 65% below pre-war levels, while US officials point to escorted exports and say main routes have been cleared of mines.

On diplomacy, Foreign Minister Araghchi said discussions on reopening the strait are pointless until Iran's demands are met, including an end to the war on all fronts, the release of frozen assets, the lifting of oil sanctions and an end to the US blockade of Iranian ports. Trump told Fox News on 22 November he was inclined to resume major strikes after the New Year if talks fail, and said any Iranian tankers trying to run the blockade would end up at the bottom of the sea. Iran was reported to be preparing 14 tankers for such an attempt; no sailing had been confirmed as of 23 November.

Iran International reported on 23 November that Washington is weighing a delay to new strikes despite Israeli pressure, and, citing Bloomberg, that Britain and several Gulf states have privately urged restraint for fear of a longer energy disruption. Iran's oil output has fallen to about 1.8 million barrels a day, roughly half its pre-war level, according to Reuters figures cited by the same outlet.

stories.headline: Houthis Claim a Hit on Saudi Arabia's Rabigh Refinery as the Coalition Downs Another Missile Over the West
stories.summary: Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said on 22 November that his forces scored a direct hit on the Rabigh refinery, a 400,000 b/d Aramco-controlled complex on the Red Sea about 165 km north of Jeddah, and also targeted a radar in Wadi al-Dawasir; no Saudi authority or the operator has confirmed damage. The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted a ballistic missile fired toward the western region early on 22 November after a civil-defence alert for the Mecca area, and later destroyed drones heading for greater Riyadh and the south. That followed three missiles and two drones intercepted on 21 November. Saudi authorities say Houthi attacks have killed 26 people since September, 23 of them at airports, according to AFP.
stories.market: Rabigh and Yanbu sit at the Red Sea end of the East-West pipeline that carries Saudi crude around Hormuz, so the claim helped limit Brent's Monday losses, Reuters said. Saudi equities, Red Sea war-risk premiums and PetroRabigh (2380.SR) are the most exposed.

body: The Houthis widened their campaign against Saudi Arabia's Red Sea energy system on 22 November, claiming a direct hit on the Rabigh refining and petrochemical complex run by PetroRabigh. The group gave no weapon type, and neither Saudi authorities, Aramco nor minority shareholder Sumitomo Chemical had confirmed any damage. Earlier Houthi claims against Rabigh in late October were never independently corroborated.

The coalition said its air defences destroyed a ballistic missile heading for the western region early on Sunday, after a civil-defence warning for the Mecca region, and later intercepted drones bound for the Riyadh area and the south. On 21 November it reported three missiles aimed at Riyadh and two drones intercepted, with five civil-defence alerts covering Najran, Riyadh, Al-Sulayyil and Jazan.

Rabigh sits at the end of the East-West pipeline that Saudi Arabia has leaned on since Hormuz was disrupted in February, moving crude from the Eastern Province to Red Sea terminals at Yanbu and Rabigh. The line can carry up to about 7 million b/d, around 5 million of it exportable, according to House of Saud. Confirmed 2026 hits on Saudi refining include Jazan in July and SATORP at Jubail in April, and the pipeline itself was halted for ten days in September.

Reuters said the Houthi claim was one reason oil losses were limited in Monday's Asian session. AFP reported that Houthi attacks have killed 26 people in Saudi Arabia since September, most of them at airports, and that a strike on 19 November damaged several floors of the Public Investment Fund tower in Riyadh.

stories.headline: Gaza Toll Since the Truce Passes 1,660 as the Displaced Protest at the Yellow Line and Hezbollah Rejects Independence Day
stories.summary: Gaza's health ministry said at least nine Palestinians were killed and 55 wounded in the 48 hours to 22 November, taking deaths since the October 2025 ceasefire to 1,661. Hundreds of displaced people protested near the Yellow Line in Deir el-Balah on 21 November against intensified Israeli air strikes; nearly two-thirds of the strip is now under Israeli control or access restrictions, Al Jazeera reported. In Lebanon, Hezbollah said on the eve of the 22 November independence day that there is no independence while Israel holds more than 500 square kilometres of the south, and the health ministry counts at least 4,390 killed since 2 March.
stories.market: Limited direct oil impact, but the fraying truces keep the Israeli shekel and Israeli risk premia tied to the wider Iran front, and Lebanese Eurobonds hostage to the stalled June 2026 framework before UNIFIL's mandate ends on 31 December.

body: Gaza's health ministry reported at least nine deaths and 55 injuries in the 48 hours to 22 November, including three people killed when a drone struck a food-aid vehicle in Gaza City on 21 November. Since the October 2025 ceasefire it counts 1,661 killed and 6,062 wounded.

Displaced residents protested near the Yellow Line in Deir el-Balah on 21 November. The line was meant to mark the first stage of an Israeli pullback under the truce, but Israeli forces have since taken more ground, and Al Jazeera reported that nearly two-thirds of Gaza is now under Israeli control or access limits. A municipal official said more than 500 housing units had been destroyed in under a month; the housing ministry counts 350,000 homeless families.
Gaza's civil defence said it had recovered 129 bodies from 39 buildings in central Gaza over a 53-day operation, with 233 people still listed as missing under those buildings.

In Lebanon, Hezbollah used independence day to reject the state's framing, saying there could be no independence while Israel occupies more than 500 square kilometres in the south, and accusing the government of failing to deter Israeli attacks. That follows President Aoun's 21 November call for both a full Israeli withdrawal and Hezbollah's disarmament. Lebanon's health ministry counts at least 4,390 killed since 2 March. Gulf News reported on 22 November that Lebanon's army arrested three people over roughly 260 kg of smuggled explosives.

stories.headline: Drone Hits a Kyiv-Region Apartment Block as Zelensky Counts 2,700 Drones in a Week and a Sanctioned Russian Ship Burns off Finland
stories.summary: Russia launched 186 drones overnight into 22 November, 161 of which Ukraine's air force said were shot down or jammed, with hits at 18 locations; in Dymer, north of Kyiv, a strike tore through a five-storey block, with police saying 15 people were missing and two bodies recovered by Sunday. Zelensky said Russia fired about 2,700 drones, 1,460 glide bombs and 165 missiles at 20 regions in the week, and urged Washington to release interceptors already paid for through NATO's PURL scheme. Ukrenergo imposed nationwide hourly power cuts on 22 November. On the other side, Ukraine's defence ministry said on 22 November its forces hit eight Russian oil sites in a week, and the sanctioned Russian cargo ship Sparta II was still burning in the Gulf of Finland after a strike Finland's military attributed to Ukraine.
stories.market: Dutch TTF gas closed Friday at €89.54/MWh with EU storage near 70%, so continued grid attacks and colder weather keep winter gas and European power exposed. Ukraine's campaign against Russian refineries and Baltic shipping supports European diesel cracks and freight insurance in the Baltic, while repeated NATO-airspace incidents keep European defence stocks in focus.

body: Russia's overnight attack into 22 November was smaller than the week's mass strikes but deadly: of 186 drones, including 72 jet-powered Shahed types, Ukraine's air force said 161 were downed or suppressed, with hits recorded at 18 sites. In Dymer, in the Kyiv region, a drone destroyed a section of a five-storey apartment building; police said 15 people were missing and regional officials said two bodies had been recovered and at least four people injured by Sunday.

Zelensky's weekly tally put Russian fire at about 2,700 drones, roughly 1,460 aerial bombs and 165 missiles across 20 regions, many of the missiles ballistic. He criticised delays in anti-ballistic interceptors and asked Washington to authorise transfers already funded through NATO's PURL mechanism. Ukrenergo applied hourly outage schedules nationwide on 22 November, and the casualty count from the 20-21 November strike on Kryvyi Rih rose to 73 injured.

Ukraine's defence ministry said on 22 November that its forces struck eight Russian oil facilities in the week of 16-19 November, including the Ilsky and Afipsky refineries in Krasnodar, three depots in Azov, the Salavat petrochemical complex, Ufa refining and the Kaleykino pumping station. bne IntelliNews counts 29 of Russia's 33 crude refineries hit during the campaign, but no new confirmed refinery hit in the 48 hours to 22 November; Russia claimed 170 Ukrainian drones downed overnight into 22 November.

In the Baltic, the Russian-flagged cargo ship Sparta II, owned by a defence-ministry logistics firm under US sanctions, was still burning on 22 November after a drone strike near Gogland; Finland's defence forces said Ukraine was likely responsible, Kyiv has not claimed it, and Finland reported no pollution. Moldova said a Russian drone entered its airspace twice on 21 November.

stories.headline: Burhan Tells Damazin 'Don't Be Afraid' as the RSF Alliance Claims Towns 40 km From the Blue Nile Capital
stories.summary: Sudan's army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan vowed on 20 November to keep fighting and told residents of Ad-Damazin, the Blue Nile state capital, not to be afraid, Asharq Al-Awsat reported on 22 November. The RSF-led Tasis alliance, with Abdelaziz al-Hilu's SPLM-N faction, claimed on 20 November to have taken several towns in Geissan, about 40 km southeast of Ad-Damazin, later listing five areas, after claiming the Bau locality headquarters on 19 November. The Blue Nile government says the army retains the initiative; both sides' accounts of other towns conflict. Burhan blamed economic strains on an 'economic war' and dismissed famine and fuel-shortage reports, though the IPC has identified famine in El Fasher and Kadugli.
stories.market: The push toward Ad-Damazin brings the RSF closer to the Roseires dam area and the Ethiopian border trade route. Gold, the main hard-currency source for both sides, rose more than 1.5% in Monday's Asian session after Friday's 4.6% drop to $3,515.40, a move driven by global markets rather than Sudan.

body: The Blue Nile front has become the war's fastest-moving. After claiming the Bau locality headquarters on 19 November, the Tasis alliance of the RSF and al-Hilu's SPLM-N said on 20 November it had captured several towns in Geissan, nearly 40 km southeast of Ad-Damazin, and later said it held five areas there. The state government says the army still holds the initiative and is working to restore security in the south of the region; accounts of other towns conflict.

Speaking in Khartoum on the evening of 20 November, Burhan addressed Ad-Damazin residents directly, telling them not to fear, and said the war remained the priority. He blamed the country's economic pressures on an 'economic war' waged by states he accuses of fuelling the conflict and dismissed reports of famine and fuel shortages as attempts to undermine morale.

Humanitarian data point the other way: the IPC has identified famine conditions in El Fasher and Kadugli, and analysis cited by WHO found about 19.5 million people facing crisis-level hunger or worse in February-May 2026. In West Kordofan, the army said last week it had broken RSF lines northeast of Abu Zabad, while a local monitor reported civilian deaths around Abu Qalb.

For markets the link is indirect. Gold is the main source of foreign exchange for both sides, but its price is set globally: futures fell 4.6% on Friday on Fed-hike bets and rebounded by more than 1.5% in Monday's Asian session, according to Gulf News.

stories.headline: Tata Steel Moves to Take Control of APL Apollo in a Rs 32,266 Crore Stake Deal, and APL Shares Slump 13%
stories.summary: Tata Steel said on Monday 23 Nov that it will buy a 26.38% stake in APL Apollo Tubes from promoter-group company S Gupta Holding at Rs 2,100 a share, about Rs 15,511 crore ($1.67bn), and make a mandatory open offer for another 26% at Rs 2,301.40 a share, worth up to Rs 16,756 crore. Full acceptance would lift Tata Steel to about 52.38% and give it control, for a combined outlay of about Rs 32,266 crore. In a linked transaction, APL Apollo will buy Tata Steel's tubes business for up to Rs 11,700 crore and its Tata Steel Colors unit for Rs 16,300 crore, about Rs 28,000 crore ($3.02bn) in total. Investors balked: APL Apollo was down 13.4% at Rs 1,837.40 by 09:54 IST and Tata Steel about 6% lower at Rs 167 by mid-morning.
stories.market: The open-offer price is about 25% above APL Apollo's Monday-morning price (our calculation from Rs 1,837.40 at 09:54 IST), but investors focused on the promoter exit and the Rs 28,000 crore APL must pay for Tata's assets against a market value of just over Rs 50,000 crore. For TATASTEEL the cash received equals about 31% of its September net debt, per JM Financial.

body: The deal is really two transactions. Tata Steel buys into APL Apollo, India's largest structural steel tubes maker, taking 26.38% of its expanded voting capital from S Gupta Holding in three tranches: about 9.91% by block deal on 23 Nov, about 11.90% at closing and the last 4.57% by 31 Mar 2028, subject to approvals. Takeover rules then require an open offer for up to 26% more, priced at Rs 2,301.40, which is Rs 201.40 above the price paid to the promoter.

In the other direction, APL Apollo will take over Tata Steel's steel tubes business, for up to Rs 11,700 crore, and all of Tata Steel Colors, for Rs 16,300 crore. The assets bring 1.7m tonnes of tubes capacity and 0.8m tonnes of coated-steel capacity, giving the combined business about 7.5m tonnes a year at first, with a target of 15.5m tonnes by 2035.

Tata Steel says the moves lift its downstream integration to about 53% from about 35% and shift its mix towards higher-margin products. It has set a long-term ambition of Rs 10,000 crore of EBITDA for the combined tubes and coated business, with a debt-free balance sheet. CEO T V Narendran called the plan strategic and said it would unlock multiple synergies.

The market's first verdict was negative for both. APL Apollo fell as much as 15% in early Mumbai trade on worries about the promoter's exit and the debt it may take on to pay for Tata's assets; Tata Steel slid about 6%. Brokers were more measured: JM Financial called it value-unlocking, while Emkay flagged the loss of downstream conversion margins and the absence of a disclosed long-term supply agreement.

stories.headline: Seoul Readies a Stock-Market Rescue Fund as the Kospi Slides Toward 4,600
stories.summary: After an emergency Sunday meeting on 22 Nov, Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il said the government will prepare a market stabilisation fund to buy index-linked products, ease daily limits on company share buybacks for three months from 24 Nov and step up policing of illegal short selling. The fund's size and launch date have not been set; a similar 10.76 trillion won vehicle was created in 2020 but never used. The measures followed a 5.21% plunge in the Kospi on Friday 20 Nov, and the index fell further on Monday, trading at 4,633.22 (-4.86%) at 11:30 a.m. KST on 23 Nov.
stories.market: Chipmakers led the slide on Monday morning, with Samsung Electronics down 4.72% and SK hynix down 4.13% as of 11:20 a.m. KST, after the Philadelphia Semiconductor index fell 10.73% on Friday; the won was little changed at 1,346.5 per dollar.

body: South Korea's economic and financial chiefs met at the Government Complex Seoul on Sunday 22 Nov, with Bank of Korea Governor Shin Hyun-song, Financial Services Commission Chairman Lee Eog-weon and Financial Supervisory Service Governor Lee Chan-jin joining Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il. The government said it will prepare a stabilisation fund, financed by contributions from financial institutions, that can buy index-linked products and other securities, and will review procedures so it can be activated quickly.
The size and start date remain open. The closest precedent is a 10.76 trillion won (about US$8bn) fund set up in 2020 during the pandemic, which was never drawn on because the market recovered.

Two measures take effect sooner. Daily caps on buyback orders by listed companies are being eased for three months from Tuesday 24 Nov, and the Financial Supervisory Service and Korea Exchange will tighten monitoring of illegal short selling, margin lending, unsettled trades and forced liquidations for three months. Short-selling value hit 1.41 trillion won on Friday, concentrated in SK hynix (159.7bn won) and Samsung Electronics (133.8bn won).

The steps did not halt Monday's slide. The Kospi opened at 4,734.90, down 2.77%, and stood at 4,633.22 (-4.86%) at 11:30 a.m. KST; the Kosdaq was at 624.21 (-3.33%). Foreign investors turned from early net buyers to net sellers of the big chipmakers, The Korea Times reported. The sell-off tracks Friday's AI-led rout in New York, where the Nasdaq fell 5.28% and Nvidia 14.01%.

stories.headline: Taiwan Bans Short Sales on Falling Stocks After the Taiex's Worst Week Since 1991
stories.summary: Taiwan's Financial Supervisory Commission on Saturday 21 Nov barred short selling of any listed stock trading below the previous day's close from Monday 23 Nov, raised the minimum short-sale margin to 150% from 130%, stopped accepting new put-warrant listings and asked lenders to recall lent shares. The Taiex fell 6.23% (2,393.60 points) to 36,033.29 on Friday 20 Nov and lost almost 18% over the week, its worst week since 1991 according to Bloomberg, and is about 28% below its 6 Oct intraday record.
stories.market: The curbs, the first blanket restriction since 2015, came as Premier Cho Jung-tai asked the NT$500bn National Stabilisation Fund, buying since 6 Nov, to step up purchases; Taiwan shares steadied in early Monday trade.

body: The FSC's new rule bans margin short sales and sales of borrowed shares in any stock priced below the previous session's close, with an exemption for securities and futures firms hedging their own business. It replaces a narrower rule from 19 Nov that covered only stocks down at least 3.5% the day before.

Alongside the ban, the regulator raised the short-sale margin requirement to 150%, froze new put-warrant listings on the TWSE and TPEx, asked securities lenders to recall shares early or not roll over loans, and urged listed companies to keep buying back stock. The central bank was asked to monitor the currency market and the NT dollar.

Friday's 2,393.60-point fall was the third-largest one-day point loss on record and took the Taiex to its lowest close in about seven months. From the 6 Oct intraday record of 49,968.92 to Friday's intraday low of 35,738.68 the index shed 28.48%.
Officials stressed the strength of the real economy: the finance ministry cited third-quarter growth of 14.4% and October export orders up 78% year on year.

stories.headline: Server Makers Seek Up to 45% More on Signed AI Orders, Putting Pricing Power at the Centre of HPE and Dell Results
stories.summary: Dell, HPE, Lenovo and Supermicro are pressing customers to pay 25% to 45% more at delivery than agreed in signed contracts for Nvidia-based AI servers, citing memory and circuit-board shortages, the Financial Times reported, as covered on 22 Nov; trading firm XTX Markets is suing Dell in Ireland after being asked for an extra $62m-$70m on a fixed $549m order. HPE reports fiscal Q4 after Monday's close with consensus EPS of about $1.28 on revenue of about $14.4bn-$14.5bn, against its own guidance of $13.9bn-$14.8bn and $1.20-$1.30. Dell follows after Tuesday's close, where analysts expect EPS of about $6.60 on $49.3bn of revenue, versus Dell's guidance of $49.0bn and $6.50; options imply a move of about 14.7% either way.
stories.market: Repricing supports HPE and DELL margins at a time of 400%-plus memory cost inflation, but legal disputes and customer pushback could hit orders; Dell's $95bn AI-server backlog and HPE's FY2027 framework of 13%-17% revenue growth are the numbers to test.

body: The FT report puts a spotlight on contract terms going into the two biggest AI-hardware results of the week. Suppliers argue component shortages leave them no choice: JPMorgan estimates memory costs have risen more than 400% since early 2024, server DRAM contract prices rose about 90% in the first quarter of 2026 alone, and a circuit-board shortage is expected to last into 2028.

HPE has already changed its quoting terms to give itself a right to reprice existing orders before shipment, chief executive Antonio Neri has said, and expects high memory and storage prices to last into 2027. Dell's dispute with XTX Markets, which paid $5m extra for price certainty on a $549m order, is now in an Irish court.

HPE reports after the bell on Monday 23 Nov with a 5 p.m. ET call. Its full-year outlook calls for 34%-37% revenue growth and adjusted EPS of $3.75-$3.85, and its preliminary FY2027 framework for 13%-17% revenue growth and at least $5.0bn of free cash flow.

Dell reports on Tuesday 24 Nov after the close. Consensus of about $6.60 a share compares with $2.59 a year ago, and revenue of about $49.3bn with $27bn. The company guided to $49.0bn of revenue, up 81%, and $6.50 of adjusted EPS. TipRanks shows 14 Buy and 7 Hold ratings with an average target of $589.32 as of 19 Nov.

stories.headline: Masayoshi Son Sounded Out Banks on a $1 Trillion SK Hynix Buyout Before SoftBank Dropped the Idea
stories.summary: SoftBank chief Masayoshi Son recently approached Wall Street institutions about financing a buyout of SK Hynix worth about $1tn, which would have been the largest acquisition ever, The Information reported on Friday, with Reuters following up over the weekend. SoftBank said it explores many opportunities and that this one is no longer under active consideration; SK Hynix said it had no knowledge of the matter and noted that a foreign takeover would need prior Korean government approval. SK Hynix was valued at 777.5tn won (about $577bn) at Friday's close, against SoftBank Group's roughly $108.7bn. On Monday 23 Nov SK Hynix fell 4.13% by 11:20 KST as the Kospi slid 4.33% to 4,659.33.
stories.market: The abandoned plan did nothing to cushion Korean chip stocks: SK Hynix traded 6.11% lower at 1.045m won in Monday pre-market dealing and Samsung Electronics fell 4.72% in the morning session. SK Square, which owns 20.67% of SK Hynix, is the gatekeeper for any future approach.

body: According to The Information, Son held recent talks with Wall Street institutions about funding a takeover of the South Korean memory maker at around $1tn. The reports do not say how the deal would have been structured or whether SK Hynix or its largest shareholder, SK Square, was formally approached.

SoftBank's response, given to The Information and repeated to Reuters, was that the idea is no longer being actively considered. SK Hynix said it knew nothing of the plan and pointed out that Korean law requires prior government approval for a foreign acquisition of the company.

The scale is hard to overstate: SK Hynix's market value of about $577bn at Friday's close is more than five times SoftBank Group's own valuation of about $108.7bn. Foreign investors hold 49.41% of SK Hynix and SK Square 20.67%.

Monday's trading showed no takeover premium. SK Hynix opened about 6% lower in pre-market dealing near the 1m-won mark and was down 4.13% by late morning, as the Kospi fell 4.33% on the global AI selloff. Korean authorities met on 22 Nov to prepare a 10.76tn-won market stabilisation fund.

stories.headline: Kalshi tells New York court a restraining order would force it to unwind every open position
stories.summary: Kalshi's lawyer told the New York County Supreme Court that the temporary restraining order sought by Attorney General Letitia James would shut the exchange for customers nationwide and would likely force the liquidation of all open positions, according to a report on 22 November. Justice Melissa Crane hears the request at 11:30 a.m. ET on Monday 23 November. The draft order would bar Kalshi from operating 'within or from' New York, where it is headquartered, and would cover sports, culture and election contracts, bar users under 21 and ban advertising on college campuses. The attorney general's office says it is not trying to close a federally regulated exchange and that Kalshi could still offer lawful futures and swaps. Kalshi says 1.2 million New Yorkers use its platform and that it wants a negotiated resolution.
stories.market: A forced unwind would hit a platform reported to be valued at $22 billion (as of 21-22 Nov 2026) and could redraw competition with licensed sportsbooks DraftKings (DKNG) and Flutter (FLUT) as US trading resumes on Monday.

body: The weekend filings sharpened the stakes of Monday's hearing. Sean Murphy of Milbank, representing Kalshi, argued that because the company is based in New York, an order reaching operations 'from' the state would in practice halt the exchange for every user and probably require all open contracts to be closed out.

The state sees it differently. James's office told the court the order would not prevent Kalshi from offering lawful futures or swaps, and asked the judge to give no weight to an August order from the Commodity Futures Trading Commission telling Kalshi to keep operating. James sued in July, calling Kalshi's sports contracts an illegal gambling operation.

The route to Monday ran through two federal judges last week. Judge Vernon Broderick sent the case back to state court on Thursday 19 November, and on Friday evening Judge Lorna Schofield refused the CFTC's emergency bid to stop the state proceedings, finding the agency unlikely to show that federal law overrides state gaming rules, according to James's office.

Appeals courts are split: the Fourth, Sixth and Ninth Circuits have sided with states and the Third Circuit with Kalshi. Sports-law attorney Daniel Wallach said an order using the 'from New York' wording would work like a nationwide injunction and that the dispute could end up on the US Supreme Court's emergency docket. Kalshi chief executive Tarek Mansour attended a Democratic Attorneys General Association meeting in Chicago last week, Politico reported; Kalshi did not say whom he met.

stories.headline: BYD vows to appeal Dutch ban on its Ti7 SUV across the EU over Land Rover Defender design
stories.summary: BYD said it strongly disagrees with a ruling by the District Court of The Hague that its Ti7 plug-in hybrid SUV infringes Jaguar Land Rover's registered EU design for the Defender, and that it will appeal, according to reports on 22-23 November. The provisional fast-track ruling, dated 20 November, bars BYD's European companies from importing, making, offering, selling, storing or delivering the Ti7 anywhere in the EU, with one week from service to comply. Breaches carry penalties of 100,000 euros a day or 25,000 euros per infringement, capped at 10 million euros. The court found no proof of copying was needed, rejected JLR's UK claims and said it lacked jurisdiction over BYD's UK company, so UK deliveries are still expected from January.
stories.market: The ban costs BYD (1211.HK) no current EU sales but raises the cost of bringing the Ti7 to Europe, including from its planned plant in Szeged, Hungary; it is a win for JLR owner Tata Motors in defending the Defender's pricing.

body: The case turns on EU registered-design law, under which a product infringes if an informed user would not form a different overall impression. The judge listed six shared features, including the shoulders, the rear-pillar panel, the wheel-arch cut-outs, the continuous glass band, the proportions and the silhouette, and made no finding that BYD copied the Defender.

BYD argued it had no concrete plans to sell the Ti7 in the EU, but the court considered that the planned Hungarian factory could build it. The company says the car is its own independent design and that it will use every legal avenue. JLR said it protects its intellectual property and acts when needed.

The ruling is provisional: JLR has six months to start full proceedings or the ban may lapse. The dispute has been running since August, when JLR's bailiffs seized records at BYD's Dutch offices; about two weeks ago the same court ordered JLR to destroy those files. In the UK, the Ti7 Excellence AWD is priced at 47,995 pounds, about 20,470 pounds below the cheapest seven-seat Defender 110.

stories.headline: WSJ ties a Singapore businessman to the Megaspeed chip network, and a successor firm that took in $300 million of Nvidia hardware
stories.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported on 21 November that Li Ming, a 52-year-old Chinese national living in Singapore, was the driving force behind Megaspeed, the company accused of diverting restricted Nvidia chips to China, with former executive Alice Huang serving as its public face. Li was charged with fraud in Singapore in February 2025 and is on bail; Megaspeed was not named in that indictment and says its business is lawful. The report also linked people around Megaspeed to Novagate Cloud, a 2025 start-up presenting itself as an Nvidia cloud partner, whose Malaysian entity received hardware containing Nvidia chips worth at least $300 million in the first five months of 2026, according to shipping records cited by the paper. Nvidia had put Megaspeed on an internal no-sale list in June 2025. None of the reports is a finding of wrongdoing by Nvidia, which is also the subject of an SEC civil inquiry.
stories.market: Nvidia (NVDA) closed at $125.53 on 20 Nov 2026 after a roughly 23% weekly fall; fresh detail on chip leakage keeps export-control and disclosure risk in focus for semiconductor stocks when US trading resumes on Monday.

body: The weekend reporting shifts attention from Nvidia's boardroom to the network around Megaspeed. According to the Journal, Li Ming worked with Alice Huang and her husband, Kang Wei, before his 2025 fraud charge; the three acquired the Singapore unit of a Chinese video-game company and renamed it Megaspeed, listing Huang as a director.

Megaspeed joined Nvidia's cloud partner programme in November 2023, which gave it priority access to chips, and moved servers to Malaysia to supply computing power to Alibaba, the reports said. Some servers allegedly went on to a Shanghai technology company in breach of US export rules. Singapore prosecutors say Li told a US supplier the servers were for local use before they were shipped to Malaysia and then elsewhere.

Novagate Cloud, set up in 2025, says it runs at least two data centres with Blackwell chips. Short seller Culper Research, which is betting against Nvidia shares, first flagged links between Novagate and Megaspeed in a May report. Li's lawyers declined to comment; Alice Huang, Kang Wei and the companies did not respond to the Journal.

The new detail lands on top of the SEC's civil investigation, which Reuters reported on 20 November had widened to possible accounting issues, and ahead of closed-door House interviews with former CEO Jensen Huang on 1 December. An investigation is not a finding of wrongdoing.

stories.headline: Russia's rules for exchange crypto trading take effect, but no venue has clearance yet
stories.summary: A Bank of Russia ordinance on organised trading in digital currencies came into force on Sunday 22 November, allowing exchanges to list cryptocurrencies once the central bank approves their trading rules. As of 22 November no venue had been publicly cleared. Moscow Exchange is targeting a 1 December pilot with BTC, ETH and USDT pairs against the rouble, and SPB Exchange has sent its rules to the regulator. Retail investors may buy only bitcoin, ether and USDT, capped at 300,000 roubles a year through a single intermediary, and must pass a knowledge test; qualified investors face no asset limit.
stories.market: The rules open a regulated rouble on-ramp for bitcoin (BTC-USD) and USDT, but the retail cap (about $3,650 a year at 82.19 roubles per dollar on 21 Nov 2026) limits flows; Moscow Exchange (MOEX.ME) gains a new product line.

body: The ordinance, registered by Russia's Justice Ministry and announced by the central bank on 11 November, sets the operating duties for any exchange that wants to run crypto trading. Venues must register participants such as brokers, asset managers and central counterparties, keep order and trade registers, monitor activity, and calculate current, volume-weighted, market and closing prices for each coin. They will report session results to the Bank of Russia as they do for other assets.

Nothing starts automatically: each venue's rulebook needs central bank approval, and state news agency TASS said actual trading is expected after 1 December. Moscow Exchange has said it needs no further licence and plans BTC/RUB, ETH/RUB and USDT/RUB pairs, trading from 06:50 to 23:50 Moscow time, with short selling banned at first. Its rouble-settled crypto futures have turned over more than 600 billion roubles since summer 2025, according to BigGo Finance.

Retail access is tightly limited. The 300,000-rouble annual ceiling applies per intermediary, and the regulator has not said whether holding accounts at several brokers would raise the effective cap. The US Treasury designated Moscow Exchange and the National Clearing Centre in June 2024, and Tether's freeze policy could in principle affect USDT used on Russian venues, though no freeze tied to the pilot has been reported.

stories.headline: Iran Is Said to Ready 14 Tankers at Kharg to Run the US Blockade as Trump Warns They Would Be Sunk
stories.summary: Tehran-municipality outlet Hamshahri reported on 20 Nov that Iran had lined up 14 tankers at Kharg Island, its main crude terminal, with crews assigned and Iranian flags raised for a run toward the Gulf of Oman, Fox News reported on 22 Nov; Al-Monitor counted more than 14 tankers near Kharg, most with transponders switched off, according to Iran International. President Trump told Fox News on Sunday 22 Nov that he hoped Iran would try and that the ships would end up on the seabed. No Iranian official has confirmed a convoy, and a sanctions-enforcement adviser at United Against Nuclear Iran said satellite imagery showed no significant loading at Kharg for some time. Late on Sunday, UK Maritime Trade Operations reported a tanker 'involved in an incident with military forces' off Chabahar in the Gulf of Oman at 14:25 GMT, without naming the ship; Euronews said the location fits a blockade-running attempt but nothing has been confirmed. Kpler data cited by Iran International show Iranian crude and condensate loadings falling from about 2 million barrels a day in March to none by September.
stories.market: Any breakout would test a market that has priced Iranian barrels out, while an interception or attack on tankers would add to war-risk premiums; Gulf News put Hormuz shipping traffic 65% below pre-war levels as of 22 Nov. Kpler's Homayoun Falakshahi estimates Iran could lose $3-6 billion a month once payments for its last cargoes to China run out around mid-December.

body: The convoy idea has been building in Iran's hardline media for most of a week. On 18 Nov the Revolutionary Guards-affiliated Fars agency ran a commentary urging Tehran to announce a tanker convoy and threatening regional energy infrastructure, Iran International reported; a Guards-linked channel later said dozens of tankers were preparing to sail for China, while labelling its own post unofficial. Lawmakers and Friday prayer leaders in several cities backed the call.

On 20 Nov Hamshahri said 14 tankers were in position at Kharg, the hub for most of Iran's crude exports. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has said the blockade must be broken, and on Saturday deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi described it as an act of war, Euronews reported, with Iran threatening immediate strikes on Gulf energy facilities if its tankers are stopped. No official has confirmed that any ship has sailed, and none of the reports give cargo volumes.

Washington has widened enforcement. US Central Command said on 18 Nov that ships taking Iranian cargo in ship-to-ship transfers could be intercepted or seized, and it says it has redirected 150 merchant vessels since June. Charlie Brown of United Against Nuclear Iran called the convoy plan most likely propaganda and said US 5th and 7th Fleet ships could intercept most or all of the vessels across the Indian Ocean; the Institute for the Study of War said an attempt could come within days and risks the loss of the fleet or a wider conflict.

Sunday brought two unexplained incidents. Iranian media, citing the navy, said two supertankers caught fire after striking mines east of the Strait of Hormuz, and UKMTO separately reported a tanker in an incident with military forces near Chabahar, close to the US blockade line. Euronews said it was unclear whether the two were linked, and UKMTO said investigations were continuing. The same day, a spoofed 'Khat Shekan' tanker signal in the Gulf was dismissed by trackers as a ship that does not exist.

The economic stakes are large for Tehran. According to Kpler figures cited by Iran International, Iranian production has fallen to about 1.8 million barrels a day, roughly half its pre-war level, and Chinese refiners typically pay one to two months after delivery, so the last receipts may arrive by mid-December.

stories.headline: Chainflip's Losses Swell to $12 Million as a Bitcoin Vault Drain Emerges; Its Bounty Offer Runs Out Today
stories.summary: Cross-chain exchange Chainflip has confirmed losses of about $12 million from Saturday's attack, more than double the $4.86 million first reported, after it emerged that 122.86 BTC were also taken from its Bitcoin vault alongside 520.2 ETH, 3.25 million USDC and 758,141 USDT from its Ethereum vault, Cointelegraph and Bitcoin.com reported on 22 Nov. Chainflip blamed a 'cryptographic key exposure' and said the attacker funded preparations through Tornado Cash on 11 Nov, then bought FLIP tokens and registered a validator on 20 Nov. It has offered the attacker 10% of the haul if the remaining 90%, about 110.58 BTC and 2,618.1 ETH, is returned by 18:38 UTC on Monday 23 Nov, in which case it would treat the case as a white-hat recovery and withdraw its complaints to police. FLIP fell 42.9% in 24 hours on CoinGecko data cited by Cointelegraph, and Bitcoin.com showed it at $0.12-0.15 on Sunday against $0.45-0.48 on 18-20 Nov. The protocol remains in safe mode with no compensation plan announced as of 22 Nov.
stories.market: FLIP has lost roughly two-thirds of its value since before the attack, and the case adds to pressure on cross-chain swap venues and validator-run signing schemes, coming a day before the Fusionist ACE bridge drain.

body: The bitcoin leg of the theft went out in a single transaction to a fresh address starting at about 01:41 ET on 21 Nov, Bitcoin.com reported, before the Ethereum vault was emptied at 07:10 UTC. The stablecoins were swapped for ether and about 2,909 ETH was pushed through Tornado Cash in 38 transactions within 48 seconds.

Analysis by Bitquery of 299,677 signatures accepted by Chainflip's Ethereum key manager since 2023 found one with a nonce far out of sequence, suggesting the transfer was authorised outside the normal multiparty signing process. Chainflip Labs says it has found and fixed the mechanism and linked the attack to a newly registered validator; validators rotated keys about an hour and 42 minutes after the transfers. A full post-mortem has not been published.

Chainflip says it holds identifying information on the attacker's validator and servers, that the attacker's addresses are flagged and that withdrawals from Tornado Cash are being watched. Deposits, withdrawals, swaps and quotes remain suspended, and no restitution had been announced as of Sunday.
It is the protocol's second loss in about ten weeks after a roughly $736,000 incident in September, for which validators later voted to compensate liquidity providers.

stories.headline: Unbacked Token Mints Drain Fusionist's ACE Bridge of $3.7 Million as Gate Rolls Back Trades
stories.summary: An attacker minted vast quantities of unbacked ACE, the token of Binance-Labs-backed blockchain gaming studio Fusionist, on BNB Chain on Sunday 22 Nov and sold them for about $2 million in USDT, The Block reported; it traced about 1,150 ETH, roughly $2 million, into Tornado Cash. The fake supply crashed ACE on BNB Chain to about $0.0001 by 13:41 ET, against roughly $0.04 on exchanges, and traders rushed to bridge cheap tokens out: between 13:13 and 15:05 ET the bridge paid out about 53.7 million genuine ACE, worth about $3.7 million, to 24 addresses, leaving it with 0.08 ACE. Fusionist told users at 14:30 ET to pause ACE transfers, trading and bridging on BNB Chain while it investigated. Exchange Gate said it would reverse ACE/USDT trades made between 12:55 and 14:15 ET, set its ACE perpetual futures to reduce-only and planned to settle and delist that market late on Monday.
stories.market: ACE was down about 20% over 24 hours near $0.069 as of Sunday 22 Nov; it trades on Binance and OKX, and Gate's rollback left some users who sold during the window with negative balances.

body: The first unauthorised mint, 3.5 million ACE, came at 12:55 ET, and the minted amounts escalated over about two and a half hours to a final mint of 10 quintillion tokens at 15:28 ET. ACE's maximum supply is 147 million, with about 116 million in circulation before the attack.

Much of the damage came from opportunists rather than the original attacker. With ACE nearly worthless on BNB Chain but still redeemable through the bridge, wallets bought cheaply and withdrew real tokens; one reportedly turned about $50 into about $17,670 within an hour. One address alone received 26.1 million ACE, and later transfer attempts covering about 1.36 billion ACE failed once the bridge was empty.

Fusionist had not posted a further update by The Block's publication, and The Block said it had asked Fusionist and OKX for comment. The incident follows Saturday's unauthorised CYBER mint on Solana and the Chainflip vault drain, making it the third cross-chain loss in two days.

stories.headline: Nigeria's Rate Setters Meet With the Street Naira Near ₦1,460 as Buenos Aires Opens the Week at a Record Blue Dollar
stories.summary: Nigeria's Monetary Policy Committee begins a two-day meeting on 23-24 Nov with the policy rate at 23%, and analysts at United Capital, Standard Chartered and Parthian Securities expect a hold, BusinessDay reported on 23 Nov, citing naira weakness and pre-election spending. The central bank sold $1.30 billion in the week to 20 Nov, yet the official rate still fell for five straight sessions to ₦1,394, while the parallel market weakened 2.33% to ₦1,458 and bureau de change dealers quoted ₦1,460, according to figures compiled in a 22 Nov newsletter by Nigerian analyst Kalu Aja. In Argentina, El Cronista's early Monday table showed the informal blue dollar at ARS 1,655/1,675, holding Friday's record, against ARS 1,550/1,600 at Banco Nación, a gap of 4.68%; the MEP rate was ARS 1,694/1,700. In Tehran, Bonbast quoted the open-market dollar at 268,000 tomans to sell at 07:37 local time on 23 Nov, slightly below Saturday's 269,250 on Arzparz, with trackers differing.
stories.market: Cordros expects foreign portfolio demand to keep the naira under pressure through year-end; a hold would keep Nigerian Treasury bill yields near 15.5-16%, according to ISSAN's David Isiavwe. Argentina's central bank has bought $291 million in November and reserves stand at $49.36 billion, with the wholesale rate well below the ARS 1,976.68 band ceiling.

body: Nigeria's rate decision comes after a 350 basis-point cut to 23% in September, with October inflation at 14.06%. BusinessDay's survey found broad agreement on a hold: Standard Chartered's Razia Khan cited naira pressure and possible portfolio outflows, Parthian's Adebowale Funmi pointed to election-related liquidity, and Agusto & Co. said the bank might at most narrow its asymmetric corridor.

The naira averaged ₦1,339 per dollar in October and was near ₦1,355.80 on 17 Nov before last week's slide to ₦1,394 at Friday's official close, having touched ₦1,400 intraday. The one-month forward was ₦1,414.99. External reserves were $54.65 billion on 19 Nov, down from a 2026 high of $55.26 billion in late October, according to the two sources.

Argentina's informal dollar starts the week up ARS 110 in November and ARS 145 since the start of the year, El Cronista said; the official rate has risen ARS 55 this month. The card ('tarjeta') rate, which includes tax surcharges, was ARS 2,054. The paper noted some inconsistent figures within its own report, and Monday's trading had not started when it was published.

In Iran, Bonbast's early Monday quotes also put the euro at 294,070 tomans and the Emami gold coin at 243 million tomans, as markets weigh reports that Tehran is preparing tankers to challenge the US blockade.

stories.headline: Private Credit's $100 Billion Saudi Opportunity Runs Into Slow Licensing and Small Deals
stories.summary: Private credit managers see a market worth an estimated $100 billion in Saudi Arabia but are struggling to deploy money there at scale, Bloomberg reported on 22 Nov. A recent $150 million financing for a little-known Saudi company backed by Goldman Sachs, HSBC, Fortress and at least three regional managers took months rather than the weeks it might take elsewhere. More than a dozen fund managers cited regulatory uncertainty and licensing that can take up to a year, while at least six said raising money for local deals has become harder; Benefit Street Partners estimates about 60% of regional private credit deals are below $30 million. Franklin Templeton's Dino Kronfol said returns could reach 16% or more, about twice those in established markets, reflecting higher risk.
stories.market: The gap shows how hard it is for Western direct lenders, under redemption pressure at home, to find large new markets; deals so far have clustered around state-linked borrowers such as Aramco and Acwa Power and fintechs Tabby and Tamara. Near-daily Houthi attacks are adding to a liquidity squeeze in the kingdom, according to the report.

body: The financing need sits largely with small and mid-sized businesses that are harder for foreign lenders to assess. Many tickets are under $50 million, too small for firms used to writing billion-dollar cheques, and some local backers prefer kingdom-based funds over international managers; at least one firm dropped plans for foreign direct investment in the kingdom.

Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's push to diversify away from oil, including into AI, needs large amounts of private capital. The Public Investment Fund has agreements with Goldman Sachs and King Street Capital to anchor private credit funds, but Bloomberg found little public sign of wide-scale progress. Saudi Arabia accounted for more than half of all regional funds closed since 2015, according to a BlackRock report citing Preqin.

Managers remain interested. Janus Henderson plans a final close of a $300 million fund early next year and is weighing about a dozen opportunities, many Saudi. Benefit Street Partners, part of Franklin Templeton with about $97 billion under management, expects the Middle East to become one of the largest private credit markets within five to ten years, with an inflection point around 2027. The Capital Market Authority did not comment.

stories.summary: GTCR, Global Payments' largest shareholder with a 16.35% stake, disclosed in a regulatory filing that it is exploring a potential takeover and is working with other private equity firms on financing, Reuters reported on 21 Nov; it stressed no definitive decision has been made. Bloomberg reported that a deal could value the payments processor at about $50bn including debt and a premium, which would make it one of the largest leveraged buyouts on record. Global Payments shares closed about 10% higher on Friday 20 Nov, giving a market value of about $22bn, or roughly $41.5bn including debt. Clayton, Dubilier & Rice, which had teamed up with GTCR earlier this month, has dropped out.
stories.market: GPN's 10% jump on a falling Friday shows that take-private bids remain one of the few supports for beaten-down mid-cap stocks; the size of the financing would test leveraged-loan and junk-bond markets where CCC spreads have widened sharply.

body: GTCR became Global Payments' biggest holder when it sold its 55% interest in Worldpay to the company last year and took shares as part of the price. Its filing turns press reports into a formal disclosure that it is studying a bid, though it said no decision has been taken.
The renewed interest comes days after a joint effort with Clayton, Dubilier & Rice was abandoned. GTCR is now lining up other buyout firms to share the cost.

At a potential $50bn including debt and premium, the deal would sit among the largest leveraged buyouts ever. The shares rose about 10% on 20 Nov and are up about 19% this year, per Reuters; Global Payments had not commented.

stories.headline: Goldman Warns Trend Funds Could Dump Up to $80 Billion of Stocks This Week as Hedge Funds Short at the Fastest Pace Since 2022
stories.summary: Goldman Sachs' trading desk said in a Sunday 22 Nov note that computer-driven trend followers (CTAs) could sell up to $80.6bn of stocks this week if the market keeps falling, and about $28.6bn even if it bounces, after selling an estimated $57bn over the past month. Hedge funds sold global equities for a third straight week, with short sales outpacing long purchases 1.5 to 1 and US single-stock shorting at its highest weekly level since June 2022; fundamental long-short net leverage fell to 42.3%, a one-year low. Goldman's panic index hit 9.8 out of 10 on Friday, and the desk called the selloff a tactical entry point while warning that the broad investor washout behind the strongest rebounds has not yet happened. CFTC data as of 17 Nov showed leveraged funds flipping to a net short of about 12,000 Nasdaq-100 futures contracts.
stories.market: The split matters for this week's tape: hedge funds have cut risk, but asset managers' equity-futures exposure sits in the 82nd percentile of the past decade and US equity funds have taken in nearly $170bn since the start of Q4, leaving room for more selling in SPX and NDX futures.

body: Goldman's desk sees two forces pulling in opposite directions. Hedge funds have already de-risked hard: three weeks of net selling, the heaviest US single-stock shorting since mid-2022 and net leverage at a one-year low of 42.3%. By that measure the unwind looks extended, and the desk said panic readings have historically been a good time to add risk.

But systematic and long-only money has not capitulated. CTAs are already short US equities in Goldman's models, with an estimated $19bn net short, yet would still be sellers globally; asset managers' futures exposure is in the 82nd percentile of ten years of data. In five past episodes when the panic index topped 9 during a Fed hiking cycle, the S&P 500 gained just 0.4% on average over the next three months.

CFTC futures data released on 20 Nov, reflecting positions on 17 Nov, showed leveraged funds trimming their S&P 500 net short to about 225,000 contracts from about 295,000, but adding nearly 20,000 Nasdaq-100 shorts to flip to a net short of about 12,000. That snapshot predates a further 7% drop in QQQ over the rest of the week.

Retail and long-only flows were still buying into the drop. Bank of America's weekly flow tally to 18 Nov showed $66.6bn into global equity funds, while its Bull & Bear indicator eased to 7.1 from 7.4 and 88% of global indices were oversold, a signal BofA said points only to short-term relief after Thanksgiving.

stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's main TASI index fell 198.46 points, or 1.95%, to 9,960.44 on Sunday 22 Nov, with 238 decliners against 29 advancers on turnover of SR2.4bn (Arab News). It was the market's first session after a weekend of Houthi missile fire at Riyadh and three days after a missile damaged several floors of the Public Investment Fund's headquarters tower; on Thursday 19 Nov the index had slipped just 0.4% to 10,159.
stories.market: The MSCI Tadawul index lost 1.05% to 1,350.18 and the Nomu parallel market 0.40% to 21,630.53 on 22 Nov; Arabian Drilling fell 2.35% to SR100.90 despite announcing a SR1.5bn offshore contract.

body: The Saudi benchmark opened the regional trading week sharply lower on Sunday 22 Nov, closing at 9,960.44, down 1.95%, according to Arab News. Selling was broad: 238 stocks fell and only 29 rose, on turnover of SR2.4bn (about US$640m).

The drop followed a run of attacks on the Kingdom. On Thursday 19 Nov a Houthi missile damaged several floors of the PIF Tower in Riyadh, with no casualties reported, and the group told investors and companies to leave Saudi Arabia, EnterpriseAM reported on 22 Nov. More Houthi missiles were fired at Riyadh over the weekend. The Thursday session itself saw only a modest 0.4% dip, to 10,159, which left the index down 3.2% for the year at that point.

The global backdrop added pressure: the S&P 500 fell for a seventh straight session on Friday 20 Nov and closed in correction territory, and markets were pricing about a 90% chance of a US rate hike in December as of 19 Nov, per Reuters.

Company news did little to offset the mood. Arabian Drilling announced a SR1.5bn long-term contract with Khafji Joint Operations for two offshore vessels but closed 2.35% lower at SR100.90, while GAS Arabian Services rose 1.81% to SR13.90 after signing a three-year unit-rate contract with Saudi Aramco.

stories.headline: Turkish Prosecutors Seek Asset Freezes on 108 Traders in the Collapsed-Funds Probe
stories.summary: A prosecutors' document dated 18 Nov and made public by an opposition Workers' Party of Turkey (TİP) lawmaker seeks freezes on securities held by 108 people who allegedly made more than 100m lira (over US$2m) each in trading profits during periods of suspected price manipulation, Euronews reported on 22 Nov. Investigators are examining whether investment funds that failed to meet withdrawals in September were used to inflate selected shares; it is unclear whether the freezes have been applied.

stories.headline: Nigeria's Rate-Setters Meet With Analysts Expecting a Hold at 23% as the Naira Weakens
stories.summary: The Central Bank of Nigeria's Monetary Policy Committee opens a two-day meeting on 23 Nov, with United Capital, Standard Chartered and Parthian Securities all expecting the policy rate to stay at 23% after a 350bp cut in September, BusinessDay reported on 23 Nov. Headline inflation fell for a fifth month to 14.06% in October, but analysts cite pressure on the naira, possible portfolio outflows and higher pre-election spending as reasons to pause.
stories.market: A hold would likely keep Treasury bill yields around 15.5-16% and bond coupons near 17%, according to ISSAN's David Isiavwe; the naira settled around N1,355.80 per dollar on 17 Nov before last week's slide, and the parallel market logged its steepest weekly fall in over two years.

body: The MPC meets on 23 and 24 Nov with the monetary policy rate at 23%, after September's 350bp cut from 26.5%. October inflation of 14.06% marked a fifth straight monthly decline.

United Capital Research expects all parameters to be left unchanged, pointing to 24% money-supply growth to N146.60tn in September and election considerations. Razia Khan of Standard Chartered also expects a hold, saying the durability of disinflation is uncertain given naira pressure and pre-election spending. Parthian Securities sees a pause now with scope for further easing in 2027, while Agusto & Co sees a hold or, at most, a narrower corridor.
The naira averaged N1,339 per dollar in October against N1,327 in September and has weakened further in November despite heavy central-bank dollar sales.

stories.headline: Four-Party Pact Puts Mashaba in Line for Johannesburg Mayor as the Council Sits
stories.summary: The ANC, ActionSA, MK Party and EFF have agreed a four-party coalition to govern Johannesburg, Tshwane and Ekurhuleni, Daily Maverick reported on 23 Nov, sidelining the DA, which topped the vote in all three metros on 4 Nov. Johannesburg's council holds its first sitting on Monday 23 Nov under a draft deal giving ActionSA's Herman Mashaba the mayoralty, MK the deputy mayor and the ANC the speaker; Tshwane sits on Thursday 26 Nov, and more than 100 hung councils must finish coalition deals by Friday 27 Nov.
stories.market: The rand closed at R17.59 per dollar on 20 Nov, its weakest of 2026 and 7.4% down from R16.38 on 9 Nov, while the JSE All Share fell 9.03% over the same span (The National, 23 Nov); the Bureau for Economic Research has warned that ousting the DA locally could spill over into the national unity government.

body: Under the draft arrangements, ActionSA takes the mayoralty in both Johannesburg and Tshwane, where Nasiphi Moya is named, with the EFF as Tshwane deputy mayor; in Ekurhuleni the ANC would hold the mayor's office with ActionSA as deputy. The ANC wants to keep the finance and infrastructure portfolios in Johannesburg, Daily Maverick reported.

Johannesburg faces water, electricity and waste crises, with level 2 water restrictions imposed at the weekend. The ANC-led line-up excludes the DA, the senior partner in the national unity government alongside the ANC.

Markets have reacted to the coalition uncertainty, a firmer dollar and a split 4-3 Reserve Bank vote to hold rates, with three members favouring a 25bp hike. The rand fell 121 cents in the ten days to 20 Nov. Economists expect petrol and diesel prices to fall by R3-4 a litre in December.

stories.headline: Kenya's Reserves Drop $656 Million in a Week, Cutting Import Cover to 5.6 Months
stories.summary: Kenya's official foreign-exchange reserves fell to US$13.949bn in the week to 19 Nov from US$14.605bn a week earlier, cutting import cover from 5.9 to 5.6 months, according to the Central Bank of Kenya bulletin of 20 Nov reported by Nairametrics on 21 Nov. Cover remains above the four-month statutory minimum; an analyst said a drop of that size is common when large import bills or debt payments fall due, and the CBK says its interventions aim to smooth volatility rather than defend a level.
stories.market: The drawdown comes as the shilling hovers around Ksh130 per dollar (19 Nov); the KESONIA interbank benchmark was unchanged at 8.75% and government debt auctions were oversubscribed.

stories.headline: Milei Signals No Change of Course as Buenos Aires Takes a Holiday After a 6% Weekly Bond Slide
stories.summary: Argentina's government denied any plan to devalue the peso and pledged larger fiscal and trade surpluses, while President Javier Milei told his circle that the core of the orthodox programme will stay, Infobae reported on 22 Nov after a week in which Global bonds fell about 6% and country risk passed 1,000bp. Officials are counting on the half-approved political reform bill and a hoped-for consumption rebound to calm markets; local markets are closed on Monday 23 Nov for National Sovereignty Day, and Chief of Cabinet Santilli gives his first report to Congress on Wednesday 25 Nov.
stories.market: Country risk ended near 1,070bp and the wholesale peso at a record 1,580 per dollar on Friday, with the gap to the CCL rate at 13.1%; the Treasury faces two peso auctions and the semi-annual Globales and Bonares payment within seven weeks (Moncloa, 22 Nov).

body: Infobae reported on 22 Nov that the Treasury is working towards a zero deficit even after a budget decree raised spending, three-quarters of it linked to pension and social benefits under indexation, and the government cut 200bn pesos from a provincial fiscal-coordination programme. Milei acknowledged in recent interviews that part of the population may face hardship but did not signal policy changes.

Government sources put Milei's poll approval at 38-40%. Bank sources did not rule out new regulations after a meeting with Banco Nación leadership, though officials confirmed none. The 2027 budget and a reform of the central bank charter are due in the Chamber of Deputies.

Moncloa reported that bond prices fell an average of 5.6% in a single session late last week and that the central bank did not intervene in the spot market after buying US$121m during the week. Analyst Mariano Sardáns of FDI attributed the jump in country risk entirely to political risk.

President Lula said on 21 Nov that social programmes will not be cut, and Planning Minister Bruno Moretti said the package reassures markets but further measures may be needed to meet targets; official estimates put the 2027 impact at R$45.1-56.1bn.

stories.headline: ASX Claws Back an Early Loss as Miners Rally and the Flash PMI Slips Deeper Into Contraction
stories.summary: The ASX 200 opened 0.6% lower on Monday 23 Nov but was up 0.1% at 8,603 by about 12:30 p.m. AEDT, as miners offset losses in the banks; it fell 1.6% to 8,593 on Friday and more than 5% last week, its worst week since mid-2022. S&P Global's flash composite PMI fell to 48.7 in November from 49.6, with new orders and output dropping at the fastest pace in over five years.
stories.market: BHP rose 2.1% after unveiling a plan, costing up to US$18.1bn, to double South Australian copper output by 2040, while CBA and ANZ were each down 1.4%; the Australian dollar was up 0.5% at 66.48 US cents at about 12:30 p.m. AEDT.

body: Australian shares opened weaker after Friday's Wall Street rout but recovered by midday, with the metals and mining sub-index higher and gold miners up about 2% at the open as spot gold rebounded to about US$3,618 an ounce by 12:30 p.m. AEDT from below US$3,540 earlier.

Among individual stocks, Sims rose 9.3% despite a broker downgrade and Lendlease gained 7.7% after denying reports of a dilutive capital raising, while testing group ALS fell more than 12% even after a 23.6% rise in underlying first-half profit. Beach Energy briefly halted trading after a weekend report that it was considering buying Santos assets in Queensland; it said no binding deal had been reached.

The November flash PMI points to a contracting private sector. A JPMorgan analyst called the bank reporting season slightly disappointing and expects loan losses to rise. October CPI, due Wednesday, is forecast to lift annual inflation to 4.8% from 4.3%, after the Reserve Bank raised the cash rate to 4.85% on 3 Nov.
